signature_length_bytes.meaning: length in bytes of the ECDSA signature present in calldata
signature_length_bytes.checkpoint: before validation, calldata as supplied by caller

trailing_poison_bytes_present.meaning: 20+ poison bytes are appended after the 77-byte signature in calldata
trailing_poison_bytes_present.checkpoint: before validation, calldata as supplied by caller

caller_is_malicious_bundler.meaning: the caller is a malicious bundler/relayer with no special privileges and no signature forgery

timestamps_bound_to_signature.meaning: the validAfter and validUntil timestamps returned in validationData are bound to the ECDSA signature and cannot be controlled without invalidating it

timestamps_controllable_without_invalida.meaning: the validAfter and validUntil timestamps returned in validationData are controllable by the caller without invalidating the ECDSA signature

valid_until_is_uint48_max.meaning: the returned validUntil equals type(uint48).max, i.e. perpetual validity

assumptions: The 77-byte signature and appended poison bytes are supplied in calldata by the caller.
validationData extraction reads validUntil/validAfter from the signature region.

unresolved.description: The intent requires timestamps to be bound to the ECDSA signature; the report does not supply a distinct expected reference timestamp value, so the binding requirement is represented as a grounded Boolean expected symbol and its controllability counterpart as the observed symbol.
The report does not give a concrete numeric validUntil value other than type(uint48).max; the perpetual-validity outcome is encoded as a Boolean.

limitations: The correspondence pattern compares a grounded controllability Boolean against a grounded binding Boolean because the report states a binding requirement rather than a concrete expected timestamp value.
validUntil = type(uint48).max is encoded as a Boolean outcome; the exact uint48 max literal is not restated as a numeric constant.

links.reported_relation: Trailing calldata bytes after the 77-byte signature are loaded into word and, after >> 160, directly poison the 96-bit packed value, letting the attacker control validUntil/validAfter.
